Alongside Zini and AG, election chief stresses election 'conducted properly,' results won't change
Publication: November 1, 2026, 11:41 pm (Israel)

Central Elections Committee Chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg released a video statement alongside Shin Bet Chief David Zini and Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara asserting that Israel's October 27 election "was conducted properly" and results will not be altered.
Sohlberg: "The election for the 26th Knesset was conducted properly" and reflected "the will of the voters." He emphasized that "suspicions are only suspicions" and that "solid evidence is required to challenge the election results." (Snippet: even if the suspicions are substantiated, "this would not undermine the integrity of the electoral process or the election results as a whole.")
Ongoing investigation into allegations of foreign interference—reportedly involving Qatar or Turkey—to boost Arab voter turnout, which reached historic levels.
Likud: a "dark cloud hangs over Israel's election results" pending investigation completion. The party noted that merely 4,612 votes separated a potential Knesset seat shift between Ra'am and right-wing blocs.
Yashar chairman Gadi Eisenkot accused Likud of attempting to "delegitimize" election outcomes, stating the results were "valid and clear."
A watchdog organization documented a 400 percent increase in anti-Arab sentiment online during election day and the following two days, with over 9,000 mentions of hate speech and conspiracy theories on October 29 alone.
Related (ToI search snippet, Likud certification bid): Likud lawyer and CEC member Ilan Bombach wrote to Sohlberg requesting an urgent meeting before the vote is certified... Sohlberg rejected Bombach's request, writing that the Central Election Committee has no authority to withhold certification of the results or to intervene in an ongoing investigation. President Isaac Herzog will receive the official election results from Sohlberg on Wednesday and will begin consultations.
